mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 5.0% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and inflation, which increases real discount rates and erodes real earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed their 12-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is impossible by definition; however, if a data artifact or revision causes this, it would indicate a severe data integrity issue, which may precede market volatility and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE increases in the same month (data artifact)
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly negative during such anomalies, or the event does not occur within the observation window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals improved housing demand, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market sentiment, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly positive at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in demand drivers, which reduces earnings expectations and increases recession risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.
